text:
maria: quick helm question — we have a chart that builds env vars from values and from ExternalSecret. When the value is "" (empty string) we end up with an env var with empty value on the pod, but we want to omit the env var entirely if it's missing or empty. Anyone seen a clean pattern?

alex: can you paste the values snippet + template you're using?

maria: sure, simplified:
```yaml
# values.yaml
service:
  env:
    API_KEY: ""    # sometimes empty, sometimes set by external secret
```
and in template:
```yaml
- name: API_KEY
  value: {{ .Values.service.env.API_KEY | quote }}
```
this always renders the `value: ""` entry.

ryan: yeah that's the trap. Helm/go-templates will render the empty string; k8s sees it as present. To omit the env var you need to guard it with an `if`. e.g.
```gotemplate
{{- if .Values.service.env.API_KEY }}
- name: API_KEY
  value: {{ .Values.service.env.API_KEY | quote }}
{{- end }}
```
That works when API_KEY is nil or empty — because empty string evaluates to false.

maria: nice. but what about when we use `envFrom` or a value that can be set via externalSecrets (so `API_KEY: null` vs `""`)? We don't want to accidentally remove the env var when external secret will populate later.

ryan: for that I usually prefer an explicit presence check + a sentinel value in values. Two patterns:
1) Treat empty string as explicit opt-in: only omit when value is nil (not provided).
```gotemplate
{{- if ne .Values.service.env.API_KEY nil }}
- name: API_KEY
  value: {{ .Values.service.env.API_KEY | default "" | quote }}
{{- end }}
```
This will render the var even if it's `""` (explicit empty) but won't render if it's missing (nil).

2) Opposite: only include if non-empty (stronger guard):
```gotemplate
{{- if and (hasKey .Values.service "env") (ne .Values.service.env.API_KEY "") }}
- name: API_KEY
  value: {{ .Values.service.env.API_KEY | quote }}
{{- end }}
```
Use whichever matches your semantics.

alex: FYI when values come from ExternalSecret at runtime, Helm renders at deploy-time using the values you supply. If ExternalSecret populates the k8s Secret after deploy, the helm-templated manifest won't magically pick it up. If you expect external secrets to fill it in, prefer `envFrom: secretRef` or let the sidecar mount the secret rather than templating the literal value.

maria: ah right — in our case we have ExternalSecret provisioning a Secret named `svc-api-key`, so better to reference it via `envFrom` or `valueFrom`. Example we switched to:
```yaml
- name: API_KEY
  valueFrom:
    secretKeyRef:
      name: svc-api-key
      key: api_key
```
That way helm doesn't need the raw value.

ryan: if you still want the double-sourcing (override via values, else fallback to secret), do this pattern: prefer value, else valueFrom.
```gotemplate
{{- if .Values.service.env.API_KEY }}
- name: API_KEY
  value: {{ .Values.service.env.API_KEY | quote }}
{{- else }}
- name: API_KEY
  valueFrom:
    secretKeyRef:
      name: svc-api-key
      key: api_key
{{- end }}
```

maria: perfect — that covers both cases. I'll open a tiny PR to switch our chart to this pattern and update the docs.

alex: ping me on the PR for quick review.

deploy-bot: deploy scheduled for staging: helm upgrade --install svc ./chart (dry-run)

maria: thanks all, PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4567 (wip) — added tests for nil vs empty behavior.
